title: Encoding Trust Suffixes in Names instead of Types
pattern: Encoding security or sanitization state via variable name prefixes/suffixes (e.g. `untrusted_url`, `safe_body`) rather than the type system.
why_bad: The compile-time safety check is erased, leaving security entirely up to developer memory. A developer can accidentally pass `untrusted_url` instead of `validated_url` to a sensitive sink, causing injection vulnerabilities undetected by the compiler.
detection: Variable names containing suffixes like `untrusted`, `safe`, `dirty`, `clean` where all variables share the identical raw type (`String`, `&str`).
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Trevor Foucher & Dustin Boswell (Chapter 11, p. 107); *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (Chapter 12, p. 124).
